title: AWL Sublist 2
description: Segunda sublista de la Academic Word List: 60 familias muy frecuentes en artículos, informes y ensayos universitarios.

cards.definition: To succeed in doing or getting something, usually through effort.
cards.example: Students who set clear goals tend to achieve better results.

cards.definition: To get or gain something, such as knowledge, skills or property.
cards.example: Children acquire language naturally through interaction with others.

cards.definition: To manage and organise the work of a company or institution.
cards.example: The scheme is administered by a small team at the local council.
cards.note: En la práctica se usa mucho más 'administer' que 'administrate'.

cards.definition: To have an influence on someone or something, or to cause a change.
cards.example: Rising sea levels will affect millions of people living in coastal areas.
cards.warning: 'Affect' es verbo; 'effect' es sustantivo: 'X affects Y' / 'X has an effect on Y'. No digas 'affect on'.

cards.definition: Suitable or right for a particular situation.
cards.example: Governments must take appropriate measures to protect endangered species.
cards.note: Como verbo (/-eɪt/) significa 'apropiarse de' algo indebidamente.

cards.definition: One part or feature of a situation, problem or subject.
cards.example: Cost is only one aspect of the decision to study abroad.
cards.warning: 'Aspecto' físico de una persona es 'appearance' o 'look', no 'aspect'.

cards.definition: To help someone or something.
cards.example: Volunteers assist elderly residents with their weekly shopping.
cards.warning: Falso amigo: 'asistir a clase' es 'attend a class', no 'assist a class'. 'Assist' = ayudar.

cards.definition: A group of people or things with shared features.
cards.example: Respondents were divided into three age categories.

cards.definition: One of the main parts of a book; a period in history or in someone's life.
cards.example: The second chapter reviews previous research on the topic.

cards.definition: An official group that investigates something; to formally ask for a piece of work.
cards.example: The government commissioned an independent report on youth unemployment.
cards.warning: 'Comisaría' de policía es 'police station'; 'commission' no tiene ese sentido.

cards.definition: People living in one area, or a group sharing interests or background.
cards.example: Libraries serve as important meeting places for the local community.

cards.definition: Having many connected parts and difficult to understand; a group of buildings.
cards.example: Climate change is a complex problem with no single solution.

cards.definition: To calculate a number or amount, often using a machine.
cards.example: The average was computed using data from all fifty states.

cards.definition: To decide something after thinking about the facts; to end something.
cards.example: The authors conclude that early intervention is the most effective strategy.
cards.warning: Mejor 'In conclusion,' que 'As a conclusion,' o 'To conclude with,'.

cards.definition: To organise and carry out an activity; a person's behaviour.
cards.example: The researchers conducted interviews with over 300 teachers.
cards.warning: 'Conducir' un coche es 'drive', no 'conduct'.

cards.definition: Happening as a result of something.
cards.example: The factory closed, with consequent job losses in the region.
cards.warning: 'Consecuente' (coherente) en el sentido de 'ser consecuente' es 'consistent', no 'consequent'.

cards.definition: To build something or form an idea; an idea or theory.
cards.example: Students must construct a clear argument supported by evidence.

cards.definition: To use energy, goods or time; to eat or drink.
cards.example: Developed countries consume far more energy per person than developing ones.

cards.definition: Praise for an achievement; a loan arrangement; a unit of study.
cards.example: The scientist was given credit for discovering the new vaccine.
cards.warning: 'Credit' no significa 'creer'; 'credible' (creíble) no pertenece a esta familia en la AWL.

cards.definition: The way of life, customs and beliefs of a group; arts and ideas.
cards.example: Learning a language helps students understand another culture from the inside.

cards.definition: To plan how something will look or work; the plan or arrangement itself.
cards.example: The programme was designed to help unemployed graduates find work.

cards.definition: Clearly separate or different; easy to notice.
cards.example: There is a distinct difference between urban and rural voting patterns.
cards.warning: 'Distinto' (diferente) suele ser 'different'. 'Distinct' implica 'claramente diferente' o 'nítido'.

cards.definition: A basic part of something; a simple chemical substance.
cards.example: Trust is an essential element of any successful team.

cards.definition: To consider one thing as being the same as or equal to another.
cards.example: Many people equate success with earning a high salary.

cards.definition: To judge the value, quality or importance of something carefully.
cards.example: Teachers need reliable tools to evaluate student progress.

cards.definition: An important or typical part of something; to include as an important part.
cards.example: A key feature of the new curriculum is its focus on critical thinking.

cards.definition: Last in a series; not able to be changed.
cards.example: The final decision will be made by the university board.
cards.warning: 'Al final' es 'in the end' (finalmente, tras un tiempo) o 'at the end of' (al final de algo); 'finally' sirve para ordenar ideas o para 'por fin'.

cards.definition: To give attention to one particular thing; the main point of attention.
cards.example: This essay will focus on the economic effects of tourism.
cards.warning: Es 'focus on', no 'focus in'.

cards.definition: A powerful effect that something has; to have a strong effect on.
cards.example: Social media has had a profound impact on how young people communicate.
cards.warning: Es 'an impact on', no 'an impact in/over'.

cards.definition: To hurt a person or animal physically.
cards.example: Thousands of cyclists are injured on city roads every year.
cards.warning: Falso amigo: 'injuria' (insulto) es 'insult' o 'slander'. 'Injure' = lesionar.

cards.definition: An organisation for research or education; to introduce a system or rule.
cards.example: Universities are among the oldest institutions in Europe.
cards.warning: 'Instituto' de secundaria en España es 'secondary school' o 'high school', no 'institute'.

cards.definition: To put money, time or effort into something to gain a benefit.
cards.example: Governments should invest more in early childhood education.
cards.warning: Es 'invest in', no 'invest on'.

cards.definition: A single thing in a list, group or set.
cards.example: Food and housing are the largest items in most household budgets.

cards.definition: A serious magazine about a subject; a written daily record.
cards.example: The findings were published in a leading medical journal.
cards.warning: 'Periódico' es 'newspaper'; 'journal' es sobre todo revista científica o diario personal.

cards.definition: To keep something in good condition or at the same level; to claim firmly.
cards.example: Critics maintain that the policy will increase inequality.
cards.warning: 'Mantener' a una familia es 'support', no 'maintain'. Ojo a la ortografía: maintenance (no 'maintainance').

cards.definition: Usual, ordinary or expected.
cards.example: Shortages of medicine are no longer considered normal in developed countries.

cards.definition: To get something, especially through effort or a formal process.
cards.example: Participants' consent was obtained before the interviews began.

cards.definition: To take part in an activity or event.
cards.example: Over 500 volunteers participated in the clinical trial.
cards.warning: Es 'participate in', no 'participate on/of'.

cards.definition: To notice something, or to understand or think of something in a certain way.
cards.example: Teenagers often perceive smoking as less risky than it really is.

cards.definition: Good or useful; hopeful; showing that something is present.
cards.example: Regular exercise has a positive effect on mental health.

cards.definition: Possible in the future; qualities that can develop into success.
cards.example: Artificial intelligence has the potential to transform healthcare.

cards.definition: Happening or existing before the one being discussed.
cards.example: Unlike previous studies, this one followed participants for ten years.

cards.definition: Most important or first; relating to education for young children.
cards.example: The primary aim of the policy is to reduce carbon emissions.

cards.definition: To buy something; something that has been bought.
cards.example: Online purchases now account for a quarter of all retail sales.

cards.definition: A set of different things of the same type; to vary between limits.
cards.example: Participants' ages ranged from 18 to 65.

cards.definition: A large area of a country or of the world.
cards.example: Unemployment remains highest in the northern regions.

cards.definition: To control an activity or process, usually by rules.
cards.example: Many argue that social media companies should be more strictly regulated.
cards.warning: 'Regular' (normal, mediocre) no es 'regulate'. 'Regular' en inglés = habitual, frecuente.

cards.definition: Connected with what is being discussed or considered.
cards.example: Students should only include information that is relevant to the question.
cards.warning: Falso amigo parcial: 'relevante' (importante) suele ser 'significant' o 'important'; 'relevant' es 'pertinente'.

cards.definition: To live in a particular place (formal).
cards.example: Over half of the world's population now resides in urban areas.

cards.definition: A supply of money, materials, people or skills that can be used.
cards.example: Schools in poorer areas often lack basic resources such as textbooks.

cards.definition: To limit the size, amount or range of something.
cards.example: Some cities restrict car access to the historic centre.

cards.definition: Safe or certain; to get something important after effort.
cards.example: Graduates with work experience find it easier to secure a job.
cards.warning: 'Seguro' (convencido) es 'sure'; 'seguro' médico es 'insurance'. 'Secure' = seguro/protegido o conseguir.

cards.definition: To try to find or get something; to try to do something (formal).
cards.example: This study seeks to explain why some students drop out of university.
cards.warning: Verbo irregular: seek – sought – sought.

cards.definition: To choose something carefully from a group.
cards.example: Participants were randomly selected from the electoral register.

cards.definition: A place where something is, was or will be built or happen.
cards.example: The site of the new hospital was chosen for its good transport links.
cards.warning: No confundir con 'sight' (vista) ni 'cite' (citar).

cards.definition: A careful plan to achieve a particular goal.
cards.example: The company adopted a new marketing strategy aimed at younger consumers.

cards.definition: A set of questions asked to many people; to ask people questions.
cards.example: A recent survey found that most employees prefer hybrid working.

cards.definition: The written words in a book or document; a piece of writing.
cards.example: The text argues that cities must adapt to rising temperatures.

cards.definition: A belief or custom passed from one generation to the next.
cards.example: Globalisation is threatening many local traditions.

cards.definition: To move someone or something from one place, person or situation to another.
cards.example: Skills learned at university are not always easy to transfer to the workplace.
